\begin{lemma}[Canonical words encode their values]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.canon_eq_bits}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.canon_eq_bits}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Canon, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.LogProg.bits_two_mul_add, Complexity.LogProg.canon_tail}
\difficulty{5}
If a Boolean word $w$ is canonical, then $w$ is exactly the binary bit word for its
value, with the first bit interpreted as least significant.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Register head returns to the origin]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.regBack_x}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.regBack_x}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.RProg, Complexity.LogProg.apply_xAct, Complexity.LogProg.rrun, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_add, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_one_x, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_succ_left, Complexity.LogProg.xAct, Complexity.LogProg.xCfg, Complexity.LogProg.xCfg_read, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ decider indices, let
$O:\mathrm{Fin}(d)\to\mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Bool})\to\mathrm{Bool}$ be an oracle, and let $c$ be a
configuration on input $x$. Choose a register $r$, a Boolean word $w$, and states
$s_0,n_x$ such that register $r$ in $c$ contains $w$; for every input symbol $a$ and
tuple of scanned register symbols $ww$, the machine transition from $s_0$ moves the
input head by $0$, moves register $r$ left by one and returns to $s_0$ if register $r$
scans a symbol, and moves register $r$ right by one and enters $n_x$ if register $r$
scans blank; also suppose $s_0$ is not a call state. For any valid input-head position
$ip$, natural number $n$, and integer $q$ with $q+1=n$ and $q<|w|$, start from the
configuration obtained from $c$ by setting the state to $s_0$, the input-head position
to $ip$, and register $r$'s head position to $q$. After $n+1$ steps the resulting
configuration is the one with state $n_x$, input-head position $ip$, unchanged tape
contents and output, and register heads as in $c$ except that register $r$ is at $0$; at
every time $t<n+1$, the configuration has state $s_0$, the same input-head position,
tape contents, and output, and register $r$'s head is at some $q'$ with $-1\le q'\le q$,
while all other register heads agree with $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Conditional skip action]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.skipAct}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.skipAct}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.xAct, Turing.Action}
For a register $r$, two states $j_K,j_{K2}$, and an optional Boolean symbol $a$, define
the action to be $xAct(r,1,0,j_K)$ when $a$ is the symbol $1$, and $xAct(r,1,0,j_{K2})$
otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Comparison action]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.cmpAct}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.cmpAct}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.xAct, Turing.Action}
For a register $r$, a state $j_C$, a state-valued function $j_{RB}$ on Boolean values,
and optional Boolean symbols $a,c$, define the action as follows: if
$a=c=\mathrm{none}$, it is $xAct(r,0,-1,j_{RB}(1))$; if $a=c$ and $a$ is present, it is
$xAct(r,1,1,j_C)$; and if $a\ne c$, it is $xAct(r,0,-1,j_{RB}(0))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Backward scan action]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.backAct}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.backAct}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.xAct, Turing.Action}
For a register $r$, states $s_0,n_x$, and an optional Boolean symbol $c$, define the
action to be $xAct(r,0,-1,s_0)$ when $c$ is present, and $xAct(r,0,1,n_x)$ when $c$ is
absent.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Rewind action]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.rewAct}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.rewAct}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.xAct, Turing.Action}
For a register $r$, states $s_0,n_x$, and an optional Boolean symbol $a$, define the
action to be $xAct(r,-1,0,s_0)$ when $a$ is present, and $xAct(r,1,0,n_x)$ when $a$ is
absent.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Comparison return run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.cmpReturn}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.cmpReturn}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.backAct, Complexity.LogProg.regBack_x, Complexity.LogProg.rewAct, Complexity.LogProg.rewind_x, Complexity.LogProg.rrun, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_add, Complexity.LogProg.xCfg, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, let $r$ be a register, and let
$j_{RB}(b),j_{I1}(b),j_{I2}(b)$ be states for each Boolean $b$, with designated states
$yes$ and $no$. Suppose that the ordinary transitions at these states perform,
respectively, the specified return action, a one-cell left move, and the specified
register-clearing action into $yes$ when $b$ is true and into $no$ otherwise; suppose
none of these states is a call state. Let $c$ be a configuration whose register $r$
stores the word $w_r$ from cell $0$. For any $b$, input-head position $ip$, and integer
$k$ with $0\le k\le |w_r|$, there is a time $T$ such that the run beginning in state
$j_{RB}(b)$ with input-head position $ip$ and register-head position $k-1$ reaches state
$yes$ if $b$ is true and $no$ otherwise, at input position $1$ and register-head
position $0$. At every earlier time $t<T$, it is in some state $s$ that is not a call
state, with register-head position $q$ satisfying $-1\le q\le |w_r|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Plain-word comparison run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.cmpPlain_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.cmpPlain_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.apply_xAct, Complexity.LogProg.cmpAct, Complexity.LogProg.inSym, Complexity.LogProg.moveInputPos_pos_val, Complexity.LogProg.rrun, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_add, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_one_x, Complexity.LogProg.xCfg, Complexity.LogProg.xCfg_read, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{6}
Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, let $r$ be a register, and let $j_C$ and
$j_{RB}(b)$ be states. Suppose that at $j_C$ every transition is the specified
comparison action using register $r$, and that $j_C$ is not a call state. Let $c$ be a
configuration in which register $r$ contains the word $w_r$ starting at cell $0$. Let
$w_i$ be an input word and $q_0$ a nonnegative integer such that, for every $k\ge 0$,
the input symbol at offset $q_0+k$ is the $k$-th symbol of $w_i$ (or is absent when
$k\ge |w_i|$), and suppose $q_0+|w_i|\le |x|+1$. For every decomposition $w_i=p u_1$ and
$w_r=p u_2$, and every input-head position $ip$ satisfying $ip=q_0+|p|$, there exist
natural numbers $T,k$ and an input-head position $ip_k$ with $ip_k=q_0+k$, $|p|\le k\le
|w_r|$, and $k\le |w_i|$, such that after $T$ steps from state $j_C$, input-head
position $ip$, and register-head position $|p|$, the machine is in state $j_{RB}(b)$, at
input-head position $ip_k$ and register-head position $k-1$, where $b$ is true exactly
when $w_i=w_r$. At every earlier time $t<T$, it is in state $j_C$ with some input-head
position and register-head position $q$ satisfying $0\le q\le |w_r|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Plain Binary Equality Run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.jeqPlain_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.jeqPlain_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.apply_xAct, Complexity.LogProg.cmpPlain_run, Complexity.LogProg.cmpReturn, Complexity.LogProg.dbl_replicate, Complexity.LogProg.inSym, Complexity.LogProg.inSym_succ, Complexity.LogProg.moveInputPos_pos_val, Complexity.LogProg.rrun, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_add, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_one_x, Complexity.LogProg.scanR, Complexity.LogProg.skipAct, Complexity.LogProg.xCfg, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode_eq_dbl}
\difficulty{6}
Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, let $r$ be a register, and let
$j_K,j_{K2},j_C,j_{RB}(b),j_{I1}(b),j_{I2}(b)$ be states, with designated states $j_C$
and $j_{RB}(b)$ depending on a Boolean $b$. Assume that at every input and work-tape
reading, the machine transitions from these states are respectively the prescribed skip
action, the action moving the input head right and register head right, the comparison
action, the return action, the action moving the input head left and register head left,
and the rewrite action entering the positive-answer state when $b$ is true and the
negative-answer state otherwise. Assume none of these states is a call state. If the
input is the pairing of a string of $n$ ones with a word $w$, and register $r$ initially
contains the binary expansion of a natural number $a$ on a buffer tape, then for some
time $T$ the run from state $j_K$, input-head position $1$, and register-head position
$0$ reaches that same head-position configuration in the state selected by whether $w$
equals the binary expansion of $a$: the positive-answer state if they are equal, and the
negative-answer state otherwise. At every earlier time $t<T$, the run is in a state that
is not a call state, with the register head between $-1$ and the length of the binary
expansion of $a$, inclusive.
\end{lemma}
